ALTERNITY.Title: Alternity Fastplay Core
ALTERNITY.Roll.StepClamped: clamped to the ends of the step scale
ALTERNITY.Roll.BadLuck: Natural 20 on an Action Check — still a success, but the Bad Luck Rule applies.
ALTERNITY.Roll.ScoresHint: Ordinary / Good / Amazing — roll this or lower.
ALTERNITY.Roll.BaseStepHint: 0 for a trained specialty or an Action Check, +1 for a broad skill or feat check.
ALTERNITY.Roll.CannotUseUntrained: This skill cannot be attempted untrained — there is no score to roll under.
ALTERNITY.Roll.WhisperHint: Post the result card to the Gamemaster only.
ALTERNITY.Roll.ConditionHint: Name how hard the circumstances make this (Table P16). Marginal is no modifier.
ALTERNITY.Roll.ExtraStepsHint: Any further step modifier, for effects quoted directly in steps.
ALTERNITY.Roll.RangeBandHint: Which band the target is in — each carries its own step modifier (Table P22).
ALTERNITY.Roll.FeatCheckHint: Roll under the bare ability score, at +1 step.
ALTERNITY.Roll.ActionCheckHint: Roll for this round's acting phase. An Action Check can never fail.
ALTERNITY.Roll.NoActionCheck: This actor has no Action Check score to roll.
ALTERNITY.Roll.AttackHint: Roll the attack check. The degree it achieves picks which damage grade fires.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DodgeHint: Roll Acrobatics-dodge. The result adjusts your resistance against the next attack.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DodgeUntrainedHint: Roll an untrained dodge — half Dexterity, at +1 step.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DodgeResult: Dodge: {degree} — the next attack takes {steps} steps.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DamageOnCard: Damage is offered on the result card, at whichever grade the check earns.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DamageGradeFallback: The achieved grade has no damage code entered, so a lower one was used.
ALTERNITY.Roll.NoDamageCode: {name} has no damage code for the {grade} grade.
ALTERNITY.Roll.ApplyHint: Applies to your targeted tokens, or to your selected ones if nothing is targeted.
ALTERNITY.Roll.NoTargets: Target or select a token first.
ALTERNITY.Roll.UnknownDamageCategory: That damage has no recognisable track to apply it to.
ALTERNITY.Roll.UseShipDamage: Warship damage runs the firepower-versus-toughness ladder — apply it from the warship sheet.
ALTERNITY.Roll.UseCompartmentDamage: A spaceship takes damage per compartment — roll hit location on the ship's sheet.
ALTERNITY.Roll.NoAttackScore: {attack} has no attack score to roll against.
ALTERNITY.Roll.NoSkillScore: {skill} has no score to roll against.
ALTERNITY.Roll.DegradedToNothing: Inferior firepower — this damage cannot hurt the target at all.
ALTERNITY.Migration.DamageForms: Alternity: updated {items} item(s) to the LI/HI/En damage forms. Check any armour-piercing weapons — they need marking as HI by hand.
ALTERNITY.Migration.DamageFormsFailed: Alternity: the damage form migration failed. See the console; it will retry on the next world load.
ALTERNITY.DamageCategoryHint: Only used for a damage code written without a trailing s/w/m.
ALTERNITY.DragDrop.NoRoom: A {type} has nowhere to go on a {actor} sheet.
ALTERNITY.DragDrop.NotEditable: You do not have permission to change this sheet.
ALTERNITY.DragDrop.Failed: Could not add the dropped item — see the console for details.
ALTERNITY.Durability.Label: Durability
ALTERNITY.LastResort.Label: Last Resorts
ALTERNITY.LastResort.MaxTitle: Maximum last resort points, from Table P6 (keyed to Personality). A Free Agent's maximum is 1 higher; 5 is the ceiling.
ALTERNITY.LastResort.CostTitle: Skill points needed to buy back a spent last resort point between adventures.
ALTERNITY.Name: Name
ALTERNITY.Skill.BaseCostHint: What a rank costs in skill points, as the skill tables print it.
ALTERNITY.Weapon.FirepowerHint: From the table's Type column. Firepower inferior to the target's toughness degrades the damage a grade.
ALTERNITY.Weapon.DamageRunHint: The damage code for this degree, e.g. d4+1s. The trailing letter names the track: s stun, w wound, m mortal.
ALTERNITY.Weapon.RangeClassHint: Which row of Table P22 this weapon reads for its range-band step modifiers.
ALTERNITY.Weapon.FiringModesHint: Which of Full, Burst and Autofire this weapon can fire.
ALTERNITY.Weapon.ActionsToReadyHint: Phases spent readying the weapon before it can be fired.
ALTERNITY.Armor.Label: Armor
ALTERNITY.Armor.ProtectionHint: One die range per damage form, as printed: d6-1 (LI), d4 (HI), d4+1 (En). Rolled when a hit of that form lands; leave a form blank if the armor does not stop it.
ALTERNITY.Armor.ToughnessHint: Ordinary for humanoids and most armor; Good for body tanks, powered attack armor, vehicles and resilient aliens. A weapon whose firepower falls short of it has its damage degraded a grade before armor is rolled.
ALTERNITY.Armor.ResistanceBonusHint: Leave at 0 for ordinary armor — it absorbs damage, it does not make the wearer harder to hit. Only field gear adjusts a resistance modifier (deflection harness +2, displacer softsuit +3).
ALTERNITY.Armor.UnreadableRating: A protection rating could not be read — use a die range such as d6-1, a plain number, or leave it blank.
ALTERNITY.Armor.SecondaryNote: Secondary damage (armor does not stop it)
ALTERNITY.Cybertech.ToleranceFull: Cyber tolerance is full — no further gear can be installed.
ALTERNITY.Cybertech.FeatCheckRequired: Past half tolerance: installing this calls for a Constitution feat check.
ALTERNITY.Cybertech.DamageRedirectMortal: Mortal damage is applied to cyber gear.
ALTERNITY.Cybertech.DamageRedirectWound: Wound and mortal damage are applied to cyber gear.
ALTERNITY.Errors.Incapacitated: This character is incapacitated and cannot act.
ALTERNITY.Errors.WeaponUnowned: A weapon has to be owned by an actor before it can be rolled.
ALTERNITY.Program.MemoryFull: Active memory is full — unload something first.
ALTERNITY.Program.NoComputer: No computer with active memory to load this into.
ALTERNITY.FX.Untrained: This power can't be used untrained.
ALTERNITY.FX.NoEnergy: Not enough energy points to use this power.
ALTERNITY.Mutation.TierMismatch: Tier belongs to the other category's ladder.
ALTERNITY.Mutation.Passive: This mutation is always on — there is nothing to roll.
ALTERNITY.ConcealmentHint: The Hide column: a step modifier on checks to spot this on its owner. Leave blank for something that cannot be concealed at all.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.HullSizeHint: Total durability of the hull, before armor. The pool the compartments are carved out of — printed as "Hull size 24" or "Dur: 24".
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.CompartmentLimitHint: Table G34’s "Comp" column: the most compartments this hull may be divided among. A ship may have fewer, but not more.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.ToughnessHint: All spaceships have Amazing toughness (GM Guide Ch.11). It is not a per-ship stat, which is why there is nothing to edit here.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.Status.OperationalHi: No compartment is taking a penalty.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.Status.DamagedHint: At least one compartment is impaired, so systems housed there suffer a step penalty.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.Status.DerelictHint: The command or engineering compartment has been wrecked. The ship cannot be flown or fought.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.Status.DestroyedHint: Every compartment has lost all of its mortal points.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.DurabilityHint: The one number that drives the rest: mortal rating equals durability, and stun and wound ratings are twice it. A compartment printed as 8/8/4 has durability 4.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.DurabilityCheckHint: Skill score for this compartment’s durability checks — twice its durability. Apply the compartment’s accumulated penalty on a mortal-damage check.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.HitRangeHint: The compartment’s band on the d20 hit-location table, transcribed from the statblock’s "Random damage" line.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.SystemPenaltyHint: Cumulative step penalty to every system in this compartment: +1 for stun over half, +1 for wound over half, +1 per mortal point.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.LifeSupportHint: One life-support unit covers compartments totalling 20 durability or less. Cargo and weapons spaces are often left unsupported.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.DamageControlHint: Ordinary/Good/Amazing damage-control systems give a −1/−2/−3 bonus to this compartment’s durability checks.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.RollHitHint: Roll d20 on this ship’s hit table. Wrecked compartments pass the hit down to the next lower-numbered one.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.FillHitTableHint: Fill every compartment’s d20 band from Table G50. Overwrites what is there — for a published ship, type its printed "Random damage" line instead.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.NoCompartmentForRoll: No compartment covers a d20 result of {roll}. Check the hit table.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.HitTableDerived: Table G50 has no printed column for {count} compartments — the bands were generated, not transcribed.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.ManeuverRatingHint: Modifier the ship applies to its helmsman’s Vehicle Operation–space vehicle checks. From Table G38, which the source scan destroyed — enter it as printed.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.AccelerationHint: Megameters per phase. From Table G39, which the source scan destroyed — enter it as printed.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.CruisingSpeedHint: Astronomical units per hour. From Table G39, which the source scan destroyed — enter it as printed.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.MovementPointsHint: Movement points the engines generate. Cross-referenced against durability on Table G38 to get the maneuver rating.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.DrivespaceHint: Light-years covered in a single starfall.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.PowerRequiredHint: Total draw of every installed weapon, defense and system. A ship may legally exceed its supply — the engineer then chooses what stays powered.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.ArmorGradeHint: Light armor is free; moderate costs 10% and heavy 20% of the hull’s total durability, rounded down.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.ComputerCoreHint: Every spaceship includes a Marginal computer core in its command compartment at no durability cost.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.DedicatedComputersHi: e.g. Good navigation and sensors dedicated computers
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.FirepowerHint: The weapon’s firepower. Against a ship’s Amazing toughness, Good firepower degrades damage one grade and Ordinary degrades it two.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.ActiveDefenseHint: Active defenses need an operator to spend an action; passive ones work on their own.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.OfflineHint: Knocked out by a failed durability check until repaired or jury-rigged.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.SkillScoreHint: The operator’s Ordinary/Good/Amazing scores for this station’s skill.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.NoCompartments: No compartments yet. Every ship needs at least one command and one engineering compartment.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.NoStationScore: The {station} station has no skill score recorded — enter one as 9/4/2.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.NoDurabilityCheck: This compartment has no durability check score.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.NoGunner: No Weapons station with a skill score, so there is no gunner to roll the attack. Add one, or roll the check on the gunner's own sheet.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnOverDurability: The compartments claim more durability than the hull has left after armor.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnOverCompartments: This hull allows fewer compartments than are defined.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnNoCommand: A ship must have at least one command compartment.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnNoEngineering: A powered ship must have at least one engineering compartment.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnOversizedCompart: Over the 10-point per-compartment cap — intended only for extraordinary alien vessels.
ALTERNITY.Spaceship.WarnHitTable: The d20 hit bands do not cover 1–20 exactly once.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SizeHint: Chassis size sets the h factor in CP = h x (30 − CON), the Constitution range, the STR/DEX ceilings, and the movement, resistance and Stealth modifiers.
ALTERNITY.Robot.Status.OperationalHint: Every budget balances and no track is full.
ALTERNITY.Robot.Status.StrainedHint: The build is over one of its budgets — chassis space, power or active memory.
ALTERNITY.Robot.Status.ShutdownHint: Stun track full. The robot is out until it reboots or is repaired.
ALTERNITY.Robot.Status.DisabledHint: Wound track full. The robot cannot function until repaired.
ALTERNITY.Robot.Status.DestroyedHint: Mortal track full. The chassis is wrecked.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ChassisPointsHint: CP = h x (30 − CON). Space runs inverse to durability: a tougher robot is packed more densely and has less room inside it.
ALTERNITY.Robot.PowerHint: Generated versus drawn. A robot may legally draw more than it makes — it then has to choose what to shut down — so this is a warning, not an error.
ALTERNITY.Robot.MemoryHint: A robot’s skills are programs. The OS holds one slot, each broad skill one, and each specialty skill one per loaded rank.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SkillPointsHint: 30 + (3 x INT), net of perks bought and flaws taken.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ActionCheckHint: AC = (2 x INT + DEX) / 3, then the profession bonus — weighted toward Intelligence because what governs a robot’s reaction is how fast it processes what it sees. A biological hero uses (INT + DEX) / 2.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ActionCheckModifierHint: Comes solely from the processor, before any perks, flaws or boost chipsets.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ActionsPerRoundHint: A/R = (INT + DEX) / 8, minimum 1, then capped by the processor and the cabling. Not a function of Will and Constitution the way a biological hero’s is.
ALTERNITY.Robot.MovementHint: Size modifier to STR + DEX for Table P8 combat movement rates.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ResistanceHint: Flat resistance modifiers granted by chassis size — small robots are harder to hit, large ones easier.
ALTERNITY.Robot.BrawlingHint: Robots ram rather than punch; damage is low impact. A base-metal chassis hits as one size larger, a mono-filament or lighter casing as one smaller. Table 5.5 is too damaged in the scan to derive, so enter it as printed.
ALTERNITY.Robot.LastResortHint: Robots have no Last Resort points at all. A Free Agent robot takes an extra resistance-modifier increase instead.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ProcessorHint: The most constraining component on the robot: it caps Intelligence, Will and Personality outright, caps usable skill ranks, sets the action check modifier and hands out the active memory slots.
ALTERNITY.Robot.CablingHint: Sets its own ceiling on actions per round — a fast brain in a serially-wired chassis still acts once — and the step modifier for Power Boost attempts.
ALTERNITY.Robot.PowerGeneratedHint: Total power factors the supply produces.
ALTERNITY.Robot.LimbCountHint: Each limb takes 5% of the chassis and gives the same 5% back inside the limb — net zero, but the denominations still round, so it is counted properly.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ReservedSlotsHint: Memory slots held open by boost, accelerator and targeting chipsets or the Grid coprocessor while switched on.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ChassisFactorsHint: System costs are paid in these, and each is rounded separately — which is why six 5% systems can cost more than one 30% system.
ALTERNITY.Robot.CapChassis: Ceiling imposed by the chassis size
ALTERNITY.Robot.EmancipatedHint: An emancipated robot starts with a hero’s funds. A non-emancipated one is property and starts with nothing.
ALTERNITY.Robot.RestrainingBoltHint: Blocks the self-learning rogue programming that would otherwise let a 6th-level robot free itself.
ALTERNITY.Robot.FatigueTrackHint: Robots have no fatigue rating — machines do not tire. Biological and synthetic-tissue actuators are the stated exception.
ALTERNITY.Robot.InstalledAIHint: An installed AI fills every memory slot the processor has, which also disables every chipset that needs a slot as a communication buffer.
ALTERNITY.Robot.QuantityHint: How many of this system. A row is a group, because the book prices groups as a whole rather than one at a time.
ALTERNITY.Robot.CostModeHint: Whether this system’s chassis cost is quoted as flat points or as a percentage of the chassis.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ChassisPercentHint: Percentage of the chassis one of these takes. The group total is paid in the minimum number of 10/5/1% denominations.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ChassisPointsColumnHint: Flat Chassis Points one of these takes.
ALTERNITY.Robot.ResolvedHint: Chassis Points this row actually costs.
ALTERNITY.Robot.DenominationHint: Buying these one at a time would have cost this instead. Grouping changes the price because each denomination rounds separately.
ALTERNITY.Robot.PowerPointsHint: Power drawn by one of these.
ALTERNITY.Robot.BroadHint: A broad skill costs one memory slot flat; a specialty costs one per loaded rank.
ALTERNITY.Robot.RankHint: Ranks the robot owns. Ranks above the processor’s Mrnk are unusable.
ALTERNITY.Robot.RanksLoadedHint: Ranks currently held in active memory. Partial loads are legal and often necessary.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SkillPointCostHint: Skill points this skill cost to buy.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SkillNotLoaded: {skill} is not in active memory, so the robot cannot use it.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SlotsHint: Active memory slots this skill is holding right now.
ALTERNITY.Robot.LoadAllHint: Load every rank into memory, or unload the skill entirely.
ALTERNITY.Robot.SkillPointChangeHint: Signed against the skill point pool: a perk spends (negative), a flaw grants (positive).
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnOverChassis: The installed systems need more chassis space than this robot has.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnPowerDeficit: The robot draws more power than it generates. Legal, but something has to be shut down to run the rest.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnMemoryOverloaded: More is loaded into active memory than the processor can hold. Skills must be swapped in and out, which costs actions.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnSkillPointsOverspent: More skill points have been spent than the robot has.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnConOutOfRange: This Constitution is outside the range the chassis size supports.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnDiminutiveLimbs: Diminutive robots cannot use limbs — they are too small.
ALTERNITY.Robot.WarnOverRanked: Ranks above the processor’s maximum are unusable in:
ALTERNITY.AI.ConceptHint: What was this AI built to do?
ALTERNITY.AI.OSQualityHint: The quality of the AI’s operating system program. It sets the Grid avatar’s physical scores, and is crossed with the processor’s quality to get the action check.
ALTERNITY.AI.LevelHint: An AI gains one level every other year. Manufacturers hold one back until about level 6.
ALTERNITY.AI.OwnAbilitiesHint: An AI has three Ability Scores of its own: Intelligence, Will and Personality.
ALTERNITY.AI.AvatarAbilitiesHint: Strength, Dexterity and Constitution belong to the shadow the operating system generates, not to the AI. They are derived, and every skill hung off them is unavailable to the AI.
ALTERNITY.AI.ActionCheckHint: Marginal+ / Ordinary / Good / Amazing. A score of 20 or more still fails on a natural 20, but can succeed on higher totals.
ALTERNITY.AI.ActionCheckBonusHint: Action check bonuses earned with achievement level, on top of the program-and-processor base.
ALTERNITY.AI.ActionCheckModifierHint: The processor’s situation die modifier, applied to every action the AI attempts.
ALTERNITY.AI.ActionsPerRoundHint: Set by crossing the operating system’s quality with the processor’s. The multitask skill adds subsystems, not actions.
ALTERNITY.AI.GridSkillScoreHint: Intelligence plus the AI’s rank in Computer Science-hacking. Everything the AI does in the Grid runs off this.
ALTERNITY.AI.HackingRankHint: Ranks in Computer Science-hacking. Half of it, rounded down, is added to each of the avatar’s physical scores.
ALTERNITY.AI.ResistanceHint: Step penalties an attacker takes. Grid attacks are resisted with Intelligence, not with the avatar’s physical scores.
ALTERNITY.AI.ProcessorHint: The core the AI runs on. It sets active memory, the maximum skill rank, and the situation die modifier.
ALTERNITY.AI.DerivedRowHint: This row of the hardware table is unreadable in the source scan. Its values follow the same law as every printed row, but no published AI uses it.
ALTERNITY.AI.CoreTypeHint: A mainframe is the smallest computer that will host an AI at all. A supercomputer only lifts the memory limit once a neural matrix is fitted.
ALTERNITY.AI.NeuralMatrixHint: Dedicated neural matrix circuitry. With a supercomputer core, active memory becomes effectively unlimited.
ALTERNITY.AI.AvatarProgramHint: The operating system generates a shadow form avatar by default. Some AIs supplement it with shadow form 2.
ALTERNITY.AI.InterfaceHint: Voice, comm port, uplink, wired into the local Grid…
ALTERNITY.AI.MirrorShadowsHint: Mirror image software splits the avatar into as many as ten shadows. Each suffers a step penalty of one less than the number created; the penalty disappears when they rejoin.
ALTERNITY.AI.MultitaskHint: Lets the AI operate one additional subsystem per rank. It never allows more than four actions per round with any one subsystem.
ALTERNITY.AI.PredictionHint: Calculating probable outcomes from multiple variables. Missing data means step penalties.
ALTERNITY.AI.RemoteHint: Lets a remote use the AI’s skill ranks instead of its own, and governs how many remotes can act at once on the same task.
ALTERNITY.AI.PurposeSkillHint: The fourth free broad skill: whichever one best defines the reason this AI was built.
ALTERNITY.AI.DurabilityNote: Damage lands on the Grid avatar: stun and wound both equal its Constitution, mortal is half of it rounded up.
ALTERNITY.AI.BackupsHint: An AI with a digital backup can reconstruct its matrix after being destroyed — minus everything learned since the backup was taken.
ALTERNITY.AI.NoPhysicalForm: No casing armour or weapons. Most AIs have neither.
ALTERNITY.AI.SlotsHint: Active memory slots this program holds while loaded.
ALTERNITY.AI.LoadedHint: Only loaded programs occupy active memory.
ALTERNITY.AI.AIDisabledHint: Written to be incompatible with a neural matrix. The AI can only run this on a remote machine, and it costs no slots here.
ALTERNITY.AI.SkillBarred: An AI cannot attempt {skill} at all.
ALTERNITY.AI.SkillNotLoaded: {skill} is not in active memory. Load it, or pull it from storage first.
ALTERNITY.AI.NoGridSkill: No Grid skill score — set the OS quality and a hacking rank first.
ALTERNITY.AI.MemoryHint: A broad skill holds one slot, a specialty one per loaded rank. Unlike a robot, an AI’s own operating system is free.
ALTERNITY.AI.BroadHint: A broad skill costs one slot flat, whatever its rank.
ALTERNITY.AI.AbilityHint: The ability this skill hangs off. Strength, Dexterity and Constitution skills are unavailable to an AI.
ALTERNITY.AI.RanksLoadedHint: Ranks currently in active memory. Part-loading is normal — the rest waits in storage memory.
ALTERNITY.AI.LoadAllHint: Load every rank, or unload the skill entirely.
ALTERNITY.AI.RemotesControlledHint: The remote skill’s rank governs how many remotes can act at once, as long as they are all doing the same thing. More can be carried; their input just lands in storage memory.
ALTERNITY.AI.Status.StrainedHint: Overloaded memory or unusable ranks. It still runs, but not as designed.
ALTERNITY.AI.Status.CrashedHint: The avatar has taken its full stun track.
ALTERNITY.AI.Status.DisabledHint: The avatar has taken its full wound track.
ALTERNITY.AI.Status.DestroyedHint: The matrix is gone and there is no backup to restore it from.
ALTERNITY.AI.Status.RestorableHint: The matrix is gone, but a backup exists. Restoring it loses everything learned since the backup was taken.
ALTERNITY.AI.WarnMemoryOverloaded: More is loaded into active memory than the processor can hold. Programs must be pulled from storage memory as they are needed.
ALTERNITY.AI.WarnOverRanked: Ranks above the processor’s maximum are unusable in:
ALTERNITY.AI.WarnAIDisabled: These programs are AI-disabled and cannot run on this neural matrix:
ALTERNITY.AI.WarnNoNeuralMatrix: A supercomputer core only lifts the active memory limit once dedicated neural matrix circuitry is fitted.
ALTERNITY.AI.WarnNoMultitask: Without the multitask skill, operating a remote costs the AI one of its own actions.
ALTERNITY.Npc.QualityHint: The four tiers the Gamemaster Guide prints every supporting character at. Marginal characters are nonprofessionals and take no profession action check bonus.
ALTERNITY.Npc.TierHint: As capable as a level {level} hero; average Ability Score {average}.
ALTERNITY.Npc.TierMarginalHint: An average member of society, and a nonprofessional; average Ability Score {average}. Use these as extras.
ALTERNITY.Npc.RoleHint: Which of the book’s categories of supporting character this is. Descriptive — it carries no mechanics.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ProfessionHint: Sets the action check bonus: Combat Spec +3, Free Agent +2, Diplomat / Tech Op / Mindwalker +1, Nonprofessional none.
ALTERNITY.Npc.DurabilityHint: Stun / wound / mortal / fatigue. Supporting cast get exactly what a hero with the same Constitution gets, so this is derived, not typed.
ALTERNITY.Npc.DurabilityNote: Stun and wound each equal Constitution; mortal and fatigue are half of it, rounded up.
ALTERNITY.Npc.SuperiorDurabilityHint: Multiplies Constitution by 1.5 before the halving — the weren racial benefit, and how several large creatures are built.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ActionCheckHint: Marginal+ / Ordinary / Good / Amazing. Half of DEX + INT, rounded down, plus the profession bonus.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ActionCheckOverrideHint: Replaces the profession bonus outright. Leave empty to let the profession and quality tier decide it.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ActionsPerRoundHint: Determined normally, exactly as for a hero.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ReactionScoreHint: A Gamemaster-Guide-only stat. The number is one less than the actions per round; the degree is set here, because the rule that governs it did not survive the source scan.
ALTERNITY.Npc.ResistanceHint: The step penalty an attacker takes. Alternity has no armour class — this is Dexterity’s resistance modifier, plus equipped armour, plus the flat adjustment.
ALTERNITY.Npc.LastResortHint: Supporting cast can hold last resort points just as heroes can.
ALTERNITY.Npc.BleedRateHint: Mortal damage taken per round while bleeding.
ALTERNITY.Npc.AttackScoreHint: The Ordinary attack score. Good and Amazing follow from it.
ALTERNITY.Npc.AttackScoreRunHint: Ordinary / Good / Amazing — half and a quarter of the score, rounded down.
ALTERNITY.Npc.MotivationHint: What does this character want, and what are they willing to do about it?
ALTERNITY.Npc.WarnMarginalNonprofessiona: Marginal characters are nonprofessionals by definition, so this profession grants no action check bonus. Raise the quality tier, or set a bonus override.
ALTERNITY.Creature.SpeciesHint: A large brown bear, or possibly a small grizzly…
ALTERNITY.Creature.RangeHint: The die expression printed beside the score, so an individual can be rolled off the species average. Free text — it is never parsed.
ALTERNITY.Creature.AnimalScaleHint: The Animal-scale score, used for anything a creature of this kind could plausibly attempt. Zero means this creature is not on the animal scale at all.
ALTERNITY.Creature.AnimalScaleNote: Intelligence and Personality run on two scales at once. The low score is the real one — no dog is as intelligent as a human — while the Animal score covers what a creature of this kind can actually manage: negotiating a maze, reading a gesture, working a pack.
ALTERNITY.Creature.DurabilityHint: Stun / wound / mortal / fatigue. Derived from Constitution, then scaled by the size multiplier.
ALTERNITY.Creature.MultiplierHint: A flat multiplier on each durability rating. 1.5 reproduces the bear, buffalo and elephant exactly; everything else in the compendium sits at 1. Note this is not the weren rule, which multiplies Constitution instead and can differ by a point.
ALTERNITY.Creature.ActionCheckHint: Entered as printed, not derived — the book warns that creature statistics are purposely modified. Good and Amazing follow from this value normally.
ALTERNITY.Creature.TunedActionCheck: Hand-tuned: the hero formula would give
ALTERNITY.Creature.ReactionScoreHint: The number is one less than the actions per round, which holds across every printed compendium entry. The degree is set here.
ALTERNITY.Creature.ReactionNoteHint: A second reaction score for one specific move, as the buffalo prints “(Charge: Good/1)”.
ALTERNITY.Creature.AttackScoreHint: The Ordinary attack score. Good and Amazing follow from it.
ALTERNITY.Creature.AttackScoreRunHint: Ordinary / Good / Amazing — half and a quarter of the score, rounded down.
ALTERNITY.Creature.ModeHint: The second half of the printed type code — the “O” in “LI/O”. Carried through as printed.
ALTERNITY.Creature.DefensesHint: A creature resists with two flat modifiers rather than per-ability ones, plus whatever natural armour it has.
ALTERNITY.Creature.ResistanceHint: The step penalty an attacker takes. Leave empty for “no resistance modifier”, which the compendium prints as a distinct statement from a modifier of zero.
ALTERNITY.Creature.NaturalArmorHint: Natural armour as the compendium prints it — a die expression per damage type, such as “d4-2”. Free text, since forms like that are not dice Foundry could roll unaided.
ALTERNITY.Creature.SkillScoreHint: The score itself, as printed in brackets. A creature cannot learn new skills or improve the ones it has, so there is no rank and no cost.
ALTERNITY.Creature.SpecialtyHint: Renders indented under the broad skill above it, the way the compendium prints “Athletics [16]-climb [18]”.
ALTERNITY.Creature.BehaviourHint: Animals rarely attack on sight and few fight to the death. What does this one actually do?
ALTERNITY.Creature.Status.WoundedHint: Once an animal takes substantial wound damage it is likely to break off the fight and move away.
